```{r setup}
source("LabFunctions.R")
packages(dplyr)
packages(lubridate)
packages(ggplot2)
packages(stringr)
packages(recapr)
packages(knitr)
packages(kableExtra)
load("data/ReportingData.RData")
set.seed(6193)
# 2013 YCB XYTE stocked fish and confirmed long-term survivor cohort
stocked_2013 <- StudyBWAnalysis |>
  filter(location_id == 592, species == "XYTE",
         release_year == 2013, event == "stocking")
TRUE_N <- stocked_2013 |>
  filter(MaxScanDate >= as.Date("2019-01-01")) |>
  nrow()
pits_true <- stocked_2013 |>
  filter(MaxScanDate >= as.Date("2019-01-01")) |>
  pull(PITIndex)
contacts_true <- StudyBWContacts |>
  filter(LID == 592, PITIndex %in% pits_true)
```

## Overview

This document validates the Chapman (1951) mark-recapture estimator and its associated bootstrap confidence intervals at Yuma Cove Backwater (YCB), using a fixed, known true population as the benchmark.

**True population definition.** From the 2013 Razorback Sucker (*Xyrauchen texanus*) stocking cohort, fish that have a passive PIT antenna contact on or after January 1, 2019 are classified as confirmed long-term survivors. Because YCB is a closed off-channel habitat with continuous passive scanning, any fish contacted in 2019 or later was necessarily present and alive throughout the entire 2013-2018 period. This group constitutes the fixed, known true population (N = **`r nrow(stocked_2013 |> filter(MaxScanDate >= as.Date("2019-01-01")))`**) against which all Chapman estimates are compared.

**What is being estimated.** Mark and capture periods in each analysis window draw exclusively from the scanning records of this confirmed survivor group. The Chapman estimator is therefore being asked to recover a known fixed N from repeated subsamples of that group's detection history — a direct test of estimator accuracy and confidence interval coverage.

Two temporal scales are examined:

- **Annual** — standard Jan-Feb marking and Oct-Apr capture periods for census years 2014-2018.
- **Sub-annual** — rolling 30-day marking and capture windows, back-to-back (capture starts 30 days after mark start), stepping forward one month at a time throughout 2014-2018.

::: {.callout-note}
The true N is fixed at the same value for every estimation window. Estimates are not expected to track a declining trajectory; they should consistently recover the same population size across all years and sub-annual windows.
:::

## Confirmed Survivor Cohort

```{r cohort}
# objects already created in setup; summarise for inline use
```

Of `r nrow(stocked_2013)` fish stocked in 2013, **`r TRUE_N`** have a recorded passive antenna contact on or after January 1, 2019, confirming their presence through 2018. All `r TRUE_N` were detected at YCB in each year from 2014 through 2018. Their passive scanning record from `r format(min(contacts_true$Date), "%B %d, %Y")` through `r format(max(contacts_true$Date), "%B %d, %Y")` is used for all estimation windows below.

---

## Annual Validation (2014-2018)

The standard project mark-recapture protocol is applied: the **marking period** is January 1 - February 28 of the census year; the **capture period** is October 1 of the census year through April 30 of the following year. The fixed true N of **`r TRUE_N`** is the benchmark for all years.

```{r annual-compute}
annual <- lapply(2014:2018, function(yr) {
  marks <- contacts_true |>
    filter(year(Date) == yr, month(Date) %in% 1:2) |>
    distinct(PITIndex) |> pull(PITIndex)
  caps <- contacts_true |>
    filter((year(Date) == yr & month(Date) > 9) |
           (year(Date) == yr + 1 & month(Date) < 5)) |>
    distinct(PITIndex) |> pull(PITIndex)
  M <- length(marks)
  C <- length(caps)
  R <- length(intersect(marks, caps))
  data.frame(Year = yr, M = M, C = C, R = R)
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  filter(R > 3) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    ci       = list(ciChapman(n1 = M, n2 = C, m2 = R,
                              method = "boot", bootreps = 10000)),
    Estimate = round(ci$Nhat),
    Lower    = round(ci$ciBoot[1]),
    Upper    = round(ci$ciBoot[2]),
    Covers   = TRUE_N >= Lower & TRUE_N <= Upper
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-ci)
```

### Results Table

```{r annual-table}
annual |>
  mutate(
    CI     = paste0(Lower, " - ", Upper),
    Covers = ifelse(Covers, "Yes", "No")
  ) |>
  select(Year, M, C, R, `N-hat` = Estimate, `95% CI` = CI, `CI Covers` = Covers) |>
  kable(align = "c",
        caption = paste0("Annual Chapman estimates for confirmed long-term survivors of the 2013 YCB stocking cohort. True N = ", TRUE_N, " in all years. M = marked; C = captured; R = recaptured.")) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE) |>
  column_spec(7, color = ifelse(annual$Covers, "darkgreen", "red"), bold = TRUE)
```

### Coverage Plot

```{r}
#| label: fig-annual
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Annual Chapman estimates (points with 95% CI error bars) for the confirmed long-term survivors of the 2013 YCB cohort. The dashed horizontal line shows the fixed true N = ", TRUE_N, ". Green = CI covers true N; red = misses.")
ggplot(annual, aes(x = Year, y = Estimate, color = Covers)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = TRUE_N, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8,
             color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper), width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = 2014.1, y = TRUE_N + 2,
           label = paste0("True N = ", TRUE_N), hjust = 0, size = 3.2,
           color = "black") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#2a7d2a", "FALSE" = "#c0392b"),
                     labels = c("TRUE" = "Covers", "FALSE" = "Misses"),
                     name = "CI Coverage") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2014:2018) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Census Year", y = "Population Estimate") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom")
```

### Summary

```{r annual-summary}
n_covers <- sum(annual$Covers)
n_total  <- nrow(annual)
```

The 95% bootstrap CI covered the true N of `r TRUE_N` in **`r n_covers` of `r n_total` census years** (`r round(100 * n_covers / n_total)`%). Point estimates ranged from `r min(annual$Estimate)` to `r max(annual$Estimate)`, all within `r max(abs(annual$Estimate - TRUE_N))` fish of the true value.

## Sub-Annual Validation — Rolling 30-Day Windows

Mark and capture windows are each **30 days**, with the capture window starting **30 days after the start of the mark window** (windows are back-to-back with no overlap). Windows step forward one month at a time from January 2014 through September 2018. The true N remains fixed at **`r TRUE_N`** for every window.

```{r subannual-compute}
window_starts <- seq(as.Date("2014-01-01"), as.Date("2018-09-01"), by = "month")

subannual_raw <- lapply(window_starts, function(mark_start) {
  mark_end  <- mark_start + 29
  cap_start <- mark_start + 30
  cap_end   <- cap_start  + 29
  marks <- contacts_true |>
    filter(Date >= mark_start, Date <= mark_end) |>
    distinct(PITIndex) |> pull(PITIndex)
  caps <- contacts_true |>
    filter(Date >= cap_start, Date <= cap_end) |>
    distinct(PITIndex) |> pull(PITIndex)
  M <- length(marks)
  C <- length(caps)
  R <- length(intersect(marks, caps))
  data.frame(MarkStart = mark_start, MarkEnd = mark_end,
             CapStart = cap_start, CapEnd = cap_end,
             M = M, C = C, R = R)
}) |> bind_rows()

subannual <- subannual_raw |>
  filter(R > 3) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    ci       = list(ciChapman(n1 = M, n2 = C, m2 = R,
                              method = "boot", bootreps = 10000)),
    Estimate = round(ci$Nhat),
    Lower    = round(ci$ciBoot[1]),
    Upper    = round(ci$ciBoot[2]),
    Covers   = TRUE_N >= Lower & TRUE_N <= Upper
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-ci)

n_windows_total    <- nrow(subannual_raw)
n_windows_excluded <- sum(subannual_raw$R <= 3)
n_windows_used     <- nrow(subannual)
```

Of `r n_windows_total` rolling windows evaluated, `r n_windows_excluded` were excluded due to R ≤ 3 (insufficient recaptures from scanner gaps or low fish activity near antennas), leaving **`r n_windows_used` windows** for analysis.

### Coverage Plot

```{r}
#| label: fig-subannual
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Rolling 30-day Chapman estimates (points with 95% CI error bars) for the confirmed long-term survivor cohort. The dashed horizontal line shows the fixed true N = ", TRUE_N, ". Green = CI covers true N; red = misses.")
#| fig-height: 5
ggplot(subannual, aes(x = MarkStart, y = Estimate, color = Covers)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = TRUE_N, linetype = "dashed",
             linewidth = 0.8, color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper), width = 5, linewidth = 0.5,
                alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2014-01-15"), y = TRUE_N + 3,
           label = paste0("True N = ", TRUE_N), hjust = 0, size = 3,
           color = "black") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#2a7d2a", "FALSE" = "#c0392b"),
                     labels = c("TRUE" = "Covers", "FALSE" = "Misses"),
                     name = "CI Coverage") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b %Y",
               expand = expansion(add = 15)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Mark Window Start", y = "Population Estimate") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        axis.line    = element_line(color = "black"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position  = "bottom")
```

### Per-Window Results Table

```{r subannual-table}
subannual |>
  mutate(
    Window = paste0(format(MarkStart, "%b %d"), " - ", format(MarkEnd, "%b %d, %Y"),
                    " \u2013 Cap: ", format(CapStart, "%b %d"), " - ", format(CapEnd, "%b %d")),
    CI     = paste0(Lower, " - ", Upper),
    Covers = ifelse(Covers, "Yes", "No")
  ) |>
  select(`Mark Window` = Window, M, C, R,
         `N` = Estimate, `95% CI` = CI, Covers) |>
  kable(align = "c",
        caption = paste0("Rolling 30-day Chapman estimates. True N = ", TRUE_N,
                         " for all windows. Windows with R <= 3 excluded.")) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, font_size = 12) |>
  column_spec(7, color = ifelse(subannual$Covers, "darkgreen", "red"), bold = TRUE)
```

### Sub-Annual Summary

```{r subannual-summary}
n_covers_sub <- sum(subannual$Covers)
pct_covers   <- round(100 * n_covers_sub / n_windows_used)
miss_windows <- subannual |>
  filter(!Covers) |>
  mutate(Label = format(MarkStart, "%b %Y")) |>
  pull(Label)
```

The 95% bootstrap CI covered the true N of `r TRUE_N` in **`r n_covers_sub` of `r n_windows_used` windows** (`r pct_covers`%).
`r if (length(miss_windows) > 0) paste0("Windows where the CI did not cover the true N: ", paste(miss_windows, collapse = ", "), ".") else "All qualifying windows achieved coverage."`

---

## Discussion

Both analyses test whether the Chapman estimator with bootstrap CIs can repeatedly recover a fixed, known true population from the scanning records of confirmed long-term survivors at YCB.

- At the **annual scale**, point estimates and CI coverage were `r if(n_covers == n_total) "perfect across all census years" else paste0("achieved in ", n_covers, " of ", n_total, " years")`, with estimates within a few fish of the true value in all cases.
- At the **sub-annual scale**, `r pct_covers`% of 2-week rolling windows achieved CI coverage of the true N despite the much shorter detection windows.

The high performance reflects the exceptional passive detection probability at YCB: with continuous antenna scanning, most fish in the confirmed survivor group are encountered in any given 2-week window, producing high recapture rates that tightly constrain the Chapman estimate. The primary source of excluded windows is scanner outages or intermittent gaps rather than estimator failure.

Together, these results support the conclusion that the bootstrap confidence intervals as implemented provide reliable coverage at YCB and that sub-annual population tracking is feasible provided scanner coverage is maintained.

### Caveats

- Results are specific to YCB and its high-coverage passive PIT infrastructure. At sites relying on physical netting or with intermittent antenna coverage, detection probabilities would be lower, recapture rates smaller, and CIs correspondingly wider with potentially reduced coverage.
- The `r n_windows_excluded` excluded sub-annual windows represent scanner gaps, not estimator failure. Sustained scanner outages during a standard annual marking or capture period would similarly degrade annual estimates.

---

Sangnawakij, P., R. Lerdsuwansri, P. Pijitrattana, P. Schlattmann, A. Maruotti, and D. Böhning. 2026. Two-way capture-recapture methods with emphasis on the bootstrap. *Statistical Methods & Applications* 35:1-22. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10260-026-00840-5
